notes: Starter pack for Indian GST slabs. Rate notifications are made by CBIC on the recommendations of the GST Council. Official CBIC notification PDFs timed out in the source research; encoded rates that rest on GST Council and PIB releases are verified_starter, reviewed on 2026-11-13. Not a filing position.

semantic_mappings.rule: Use for supplies that take the 18% GST slab, the ordinary rate both before and after the 56th Council rationalisation.
Use for supplies that take the 5% merit / lower slab. From 22 September 2025 this slab is widened; it is still reduced, not standard.
Use only for historical supplies that took the 12% slab through 21 September 2025. Do not use it for supplies on or after 22 September 2025.

Use for de-merit goods that moved from 28% to 40% on 22 September 2025. Do not use it for cigarettes, chewing tobacco such as zarda, unmanufactured tobacco, or beedi on a date from 22 September 2025 through 31 January 2026: those goods kept their previous GST rate plus compensation cess, and that transition-period rate is not encoded. From 1 February 2026 the 40% version covers the notified tobacco and pan masala goods other than bidis and other than tobacco leaves. Do not use luxury for compensation cess.

Use for the domestic nil slab (rate 0) described in the Council / PIB materials, including UHT milk from 22 September 2025. Chargeability is exempt and input tax is not creditable. Do not use this for IGST Act s 16 export or SEZ zero-rating, which is not encoded.
Use for supplies that the exemption notifications relieve from GST. The lists themselves are not copied here.

rates.notes: From 1 February 2026, pan masala, manufactured tobacco products other than bidis, cigarettes, and nicotine inhalation products move to 40%, and compensation cess on those goods is nil, as summarised in the GST Council December 2025 newsletter (Notifications 19/2025-CT(Rate) and 03/2025-Compensation Cess (Rate), dated 31 December 2025, not opened). Unmanufactured tobacco in that 40% scope excludes tobacco leaves: the PIB FAQ states tobacco leaves were already at 5%, and that 5% leaf rate is not encoded here. Bidi is described in the 56th Council annexure as moving from 28% to 18%, not to 40%. Whether any goods remain at 28% after this date was not confirmed.

treatments.notes: 28% through 21 September 2025, then 40%. Compensation cess, where it still applies, is a separate levy and is not encoded as a rate in this pack.
